Anantara-branded villas in Bali up for sale with prices from US$700,000
article:
A collection of branded residences located in Bali, Indonesia, is up for grabs. Anantara Residences Ubud Bali launched for sale this month, offering 15 one- and two-bedroom pool villas.

Developed by Minor International (which owns the Anantara brand) and state-owned Indonesian developer PT Wijaya Karya Realty, the development neighbours Anantara Ubud Bali Resort, an 85-key hotel the partners opened in October 2024.

The resort and residences are located in Payangan, about 35 minutes north of central Ubud and two hours from Denpasar International Airport. The Payangan district is known for its picturesque highlands, river valleys and rainforests.

Indicative prices of the villas start from an estimated US$700,000 (around $895,000).

One-bedroom villas measure 1,163 sq ft. Each unit features a private infinity pool with views overlooking the forest.

Two-bedroom villas, each spanning 1,765 sq ft, also come with a private pool. Designed for families, they feature an expansive layout, along with en suite bathrooms in both bedrooms.

Jakarta-based architecture firm Aboday designed the villas, with interiors crafted by Malaysia’s EDC International.

The villas include 24-hour manned security, fibre-optic internet and underground utilities, emergency power supply, and rainwater recycling systems for landscaping.

Owners will have access to resort amenities, which include a spa, fitness centre, kids’ and teens’ clubs, and around-the-clock butler services.

Qualified owners will have the option to join the development’s resort-managed rental programme. Anantara will fully manage the property on behalf of owners, according to Minor International.

With a fully compliant rental model operated by Anantara, the development gives owners access to global demand, expert revenue management and hassle-free property care,” said Micah Tamthai, the group’s COO of lifestyle and real estate.

Tamthai believes the residences, designed for high-net-worth individuals, will appeal not only to investors but also to “wellness seekers and culture aficionados who want to live, not just visit, Bali”.

"We’re seeing strong local demand from Jakarta and Surabaya, as well as from buyers in Singapore, Hong Kong, Australia, the US and the UK, all looking to diversify their portfolios with branded real estate in Southeast Asia," he said.

title: Ground-floor strata commercial unit on Keong Saik Road for sale at $11 mil
article:
A ground-floor strata commercial unit at 6 Keong Saik Road is being offered for sale through an expression of interest (EOI) exercise. The 999-year leasehold unit measuring 1,389 sq ft is priced from $11 million, or $7,919 psf.

The unit is approved for restaurant use, according to Steward Asia (a unit of PropNex), which is marketing the property. French restaurant Loulou formerly occupied the unit, but it has ceased operations and vacated the space.

The unit sits on the ground floor of a strata-titled three-storey shophouse. It last changed hands for $8.5 million ($6,121 psf) in September 2024, based on lodged caveats.

The latest Keong Saik Road commercial transaction was for a freehold shophouse that fetched $16 million in June, caveats show. Before that, Steward Asia had brokered the deal for another freehold shophouse at 3 Keong Saik Road for $22 million in May.

“At $11 million, 6 Keong Saik Road gives investors a 999-year lease on the same street, with F&B approval already in place to attract tenants and owner-occupiers,” said Raelyn Lee, Steward Asia’s listing manager.

Steward Asia co-founder Loyalle Chin added that no freehold or 999-year shophouse in the CBD and Chinatown has sold below $15 million since 2025.

The EOI will close at 3pm on Oct 30.

title: Keppel DC REIT vs CICT: Which REIT Would I Buy Today?
article:

passive income from property
without buying any yourself.
Two of the best known, though, collect that income from two very different property types.
Keppel DC REIT
(SGX: AJBU), or KDCREIT, offers exposure to secular technology trends (AI and cloud computing) through its various
data centres
.
On the other hand,
CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust
(SGX: C38U), or CICT, takes a more traditional route with malls, offices and integrated developments.
Let’s find out which one offers the better risk-reward balance today.

Understanding the Two REITs
As at 30 June 2026 (1H2026), KDCREIT owns 25 data centres across ten countries, with Singapore the biggest market at 62.8% of assets under management.
Internet companies are the main customers, supplying 70.4% of rental income.
Colocation leases, which bring in roughly 74% of the rent, last only 2.8 years on average, so renewals come around quickly.
Occupancy stands at 92.5%, but a tenant has vacated the Cardiff site, and without it the figure would be 95.3%.
Customers have already signed up for about 95% of its power capacity.
At renewal, rents rose by about 10% on average in 1H2026, and the REIT grew by buying or upgrading data centres.
Almost all of CICT’s portfolio is in Singapore.
At the end of 1H2026 (30 June 2026), 97.7% of retail space was occupied, against 94.4% of offices and 95.5% of integrated developments.
Its retail leases have a weighted average expiry of just 2.0 years, so CICT can reprice shop space regularly.
Rents on renewed retail leases rose 4.0%, and on office leases 6.5%, in 1H2026, supporting CICT’s distributable income.

Both raised DPU in 1H2026, by 11.3% at KDCREIT and 7.1% at CICT.
Since FY2021, though, CICT’s DPU has grown 11.3%, or 2.7% a year, and has risen every year.
KDCREIT grew about 1.3% a year, with a single decline, in 2023.
Neither REIT splits organic growth from acquisitions, but unit counts help.
KDCREIT’s unit count has risen substantially over the past few years as the REIT used equity to buy assets.
In 1H2026, its distributable income rose 18.5% but DPU only 11.3%.
Similarly, CICT issued new units to help fund its latest acquisition, Paragon.
Concentration matters for sustainability.
A single hyperscaler, meaning a very large cloud operator, supplies more than 40% of KDCREIT’s rental income.
Keppel DC Singapore 1 is a weak spot: it was only 46.5% occupied at 30 June 2026, and its contracts averaged just 1.1 years.

KDCREIT wins four of five measures, but its shorter 3.1-year average debt term means it will need to refinance its S$2.3 billion of debt sooner than CICT.
A 0.25-percentage-point rate change moves KDCREIT’s DPU by about 0.3%, roughly 1.2% for a full percentage point.
For CICT, a one-percentage-point rate rise would cut DPU by about S$0.0027, or around 2%.
In September 2026, KDCREIT agreed to buy stakes in two Tokyo data centres for about S$1.37 billion, partly funded by a S$625 million placement of new units at S$2.10 each.
Aggregate leverage is expected to rise from 34.0% to about 38.0%, just under its 40% internal leverage limit.
CICT funded Paragon with a S$750 million placement at S$2.30 a unit, debt, and the S$2.476 billion sale of Asia Square Tower 2.
Growth Potential: Data Centres vs Retail and Offices
KDCREIT has the stronger tailwind, with reversions of about 10% for 1H2026 and steady cloud and AI demand.
The risks are power supply, reliance on one large client, capital spending and shifts in AI workloads.
Faster distributable income growth likely needs acquisitions and, as the Tokyo deal shows, fresh equity.
CICT’s growth is slower but easier to see.
Paragon, bought at a 3.9% yield, adds about 1.7% to full-year DPU, with roughly half showing up in 2027.
Add organic growth of 1.5% to 2%, and DPU growth of about 2.5% in 2027 looks plausible.
Asset enhancement initiatives (AEIs) at Tampines Mall and Lot One could add an estimated 0.5% or so, based on their capex and expected returns.
Over the long term, KDCREIT has the higher ceiling thanks to its structural tailwind, but the REIT is dependent on power, a few clients and fresh equity.
CICT grows slowly from a diversified base.

KDCREIT trades 24% above NAV and CICT 3% above.
A premium can be justified by faster growth and a cleaner balance sheet, but it raises expectations.
KDCREIT’s DPU grew just 1.3% a year over four years, and part of the latest jump came from buying out the remaining stakes in Keppel DC Singapore 3 and 4, not just rent growth.
Higher interest costs on acquisition loans offset part of the gain.
Both trade near the bottom of their 52-week price ranges, so both yields sit near the top, CICT’s more so.
Total return is roughly yield plus
DPU growth
.
Assume yields stay put for three years.
If KDCREIT’s DPU grows 5% a year (well above its 1.3% track record) and CICT’s grows 3%, KDCREIT returns about 10% a year and CICT about 8.4%.
But KDCREIT trades at 1.24 times NAV.
If that premium shrinks to 1.10 times over three years, its return falls to about 6%, and it would need DPU growth of about 7% a year to keep pace with CICT.
At its historical growth rate, KDCREIT would trail CICT even if its premium held.
Get Smart: Which REIT Would I Buy Today?
KDCREIT’s case rests on its growth and its balance sheet, with 1H2026 DPU up 11.3% and leverage of 34%, rising to about 38% after the Tokyo deal.
CICT’s case rests on income and price, with a 5.42% yield and a DPU that has risen every year since FY2021.
Which REIT to buy depends on whether you’re comfortable trading lower income today for faster growth (KDCREIT), or prefer stable income diversified across multiple tenants and property types (CICT).

title: DBS, OCBC, UOB: Singapore Banks Are Cheaper, But Are They a Bargain?
article:
Earlier this month, Citi downgraded
Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation
(SGX: O39), or OCBC, from Neutral to Sell, with a target price of S$27.50.
In response, investors hit the sell button.
OCBC shares tumbled 5.9% in a single session.
DBS Group
(SGX: D05) and
United Overseas Bank
(SGX: U11), or UOB, slid alongside it.
The message was simple: sell OCBC.
But here’s what most investors missed.
Divide Citi’s target price by OCBC’s book value (as at 30 June 2026) of S$13.73 per share, and you get a surprising ratio: two times book.
Let me put that in perspective.
Over the past decade, OCBC shares have traded at an average of 1.22 times book value.
Between 2017 and 2025, the ratio was below 1.5 times most of the time.
In other words, Citi’s bearish target still values OCBC at more than 60% above its long-term average multiple.
Not long ago, a target like that would have read as wildly optimistic.
So if even the Sell call looks expensive by historical standards, what does that tell you about Singapore’s banks today?
The answer is: bank shares are indeed cheaper.
But they are still not cheap.
A lower share price does not make a bargain.
When shares are trading at higher multiples, the banks have more to live up to.
And that hasn’t changed.

DBS at a Record High: Buy, Hold or Wait for a Pullback?
Cheaper, but not cheap
Let’s start with the numbers.

Source: Company filings, Fiscal.ai, author’s calculations. Based on OCBC’s share price of S$29.00 as at 16 October 2026 and book value of S$13.73 as at 30 June 2026. The current yield includes OCBC’s special dividend; the figure in brackets excludes it.
OCBC, even after its recent tumble, sits at about 2.1 times book.
That’s over 70% above its long-term average.
For most of the past decade, OCBC traded close to its average, marked by the dashed red line.
That changed from late 2024 onwards, when the shares broke well clear of their historical range.
Notice the deep dip in 2020 as well.
The dividend yield points the same way.
At S$29, OCBC yields 3.6%, below its 10-year average of 4.5%.
But that figure includes a special dividend.
Count only the ordinary dividend, and the yield falls to 3.1%.
Even at Citi’s S$27.50 target, OCBC would yield 3.8%, still below its long-term average.
The price of a bargain
For a bank to trade at a truly cheap valuation, there’s a trade-off you have to accept.
Something bad usually has to happen first.
If you’re a deep value investor, you would wait for OCBC to trade at or below its book value of S$13.73.
But you won’t know when that will be.
It has happened only around three times in the past 20 years.
The sharpest dip of the past decade came during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020.
That’s the dip you saw in the chart earlier.
Related articles:
3 Singapore Blue-Chip Stocks Hitting 52-Week Highs: Are They Still Buys?
Get Smart: Record Profits, Bigger Dividends – But Are the Banks Still a Buy?
Get Smart: Optimise for a calm mind
Let’s return to where we started.
Citi’s Sell call on OCBC sent the shares tumbling.
Yet behind the headline was a model whose target still valued OCBC at two times book.
If you sold on the headline alone, you acted on someone else’s assumptions.
Here’s what I’d suggest instead.
First, know what you’re paying for.
At today’s prices, there’s still a fair bit of optimism built into bank shares.
In other words, the business has to live up to it.
Second, decide what kind of investor you are, then work out your price from there.
A deep value investor, an income investor, and an analyst can all arrive at different prices for the same bank.
And finally, do not optimise for performance.
Optimise for a calm mind.
Genuinely cheap bank shares only show up when the news is frightening.
When that day comes again, as it did in March 2020, a calm mind is the best strategy you can have.

title: Top 3 REITs to Watch This Week
article:
Most
real estate investment trust
(REIT) investors read results the same way.
They find the distribution per unit (DPU), check whether it went up and move on.
That habit can mislead.
Three Singapore REITs report later this month, and each gave investors a reason to read past the headline last time.
Frasers Centrepoint Trust
(SGX: J69U), or FCT, and
Suntec REIT
(SGX: T82U) report on 22 October 2026.
CapitaLand China Trust
(SGX: AU8U), or CLCT, follows on 23 October.
What will FCT’s first financial figures since the half-year reveal?
FCT
is the largest owner of suburban retail space in Singapore.
It owns nine malls and one office property, with assets under management (AUM) of S$8.4 billion.
The manager reports financial figures only at the half-year and full-year marks.
Its business update for the third quarter of FY2026, released on 27 July 2026, carried no net property income (NPI) or DPU.
Retail committed occupancy stood at 99.6% as at 30 June 2026, down from 99.8% three months earlier.
The latest figure excluded Hougang Mall and NEX, both undergoing asset enhancement initiatives (AEIs).
The Hougang Mall AEI was over 98% committed and on track for completion in September 2026, while NEX’s Phase 1 had reached 87% pre-commitment.
Watch how occupancy moves once these malls return to the count.
Shopper traffic rose 2.4% year on year (YoY) in the quarter.
Tenancy churn and refresh held tenants’ sales growth to 0.2%.
FCT did not disclose rental reversion, so look for that figure in the full-year release.
Aggregate leverage stood at 40.4%.
The average cost of debt fell to 3.0% from 3.2% in the preceding quarter.
FCT also proposed to divest White Sands for S$467.0 million, an 8.4% premium to valuation.
The manager earmarked net proceeds of S$454.1 million for debt repayment, which would lower pro forma leverage to 36.5%.
On the flip side, FCT would give up White Sands’ rental income.
Investors should weigh the interest saved against the income lost.
FCT has a 50% interest in the commercial component of a consortium bid for the Bayshore Drive site at a tender price of S$2.1 billion.
Any funding details will shape where leverage goes next.
Related articles:
CICT, FCT or Mapletree Industrial Trust: Which REIT Is the Best Buy Today?
Frasers Property’s Capital Recycling: What It Means for FCT and FLCT
Can Suntec REIT’s DPU growth outlast its one-offs?
Suntec REIT is Singapore’s first composite REIT and owns 10 properties across Singapore, Australia and the UK, with AUM of S$12.2 billion.
For the first half of 2026 (1H2026), DPU rose 24.8% YoY to S$0.039.
Gross revenue grew 1.9% to S$238.9 million, but NPI slipped 0.3% to S$159.0 million.
In other words, DPU grew far faster than property income.
The manager credited stronger Singapore office and retail performance.
A S$9.4 million reduction in financing costs also helped, as did the absence of a S$3.4 million Australian withholding tax provision.
That last item reflects a prior-year comparison, not an operational gain.
Committed occupancy for both Singapore office and retail stood at 99.5% as at 30 June 2026.
Rental reversion came in at 10.1% for office and 10.7% for retail.
Aggregate leverage rose to 43.0%, the highest of the three REITs here.
On 22 October, check whether NPI returns to growth and whether Singapore reversions stay positive.
If the release includes DPU, compare its growth with NPI before reading too much into it.
Related articles:
REITs Underperforming in 2026 vs STI – Is It Time to Buy?
Suntec REIT vs MPACT: Which Offers Better Value for Investors?
When will CLCT’s same-store gains show up in the headline?
CLCT is the largest China-focused Singapore REIT.
It owns 17 properties in China across retail malls, business parks and logistics parks, with AUM of S$4.6 billion.
Its 1H2026 headline numbers looked weak.
Gross revenue fell 5.2% YoY to RMB822.6 million.
NPI declined 3.3% to RMB561.0 million and DPU slipped 1.6% to S$0.0245.
Exclude CapitaMall Yuhuating, which CLCT divested in October 2025, and the picture improves.
On that same-store basis, revenue eased only 0.2%.
NPI grew 1.3% and DPU rose 2.9%.
The Yuhuating drag should fade once YoY comparisons move past the divestment.
Business parks remain the weak spot.
Committed occupancy fell to 85.1% from 86.9% a year ago, with rental reversion at -12.0%.
Retail reversion stood at -2.7%, though retail occupancy improved to 97.3% from 96.9%.
Logistics shows the most encouraging trend.
Occupancy rose to 99.0% from 96.6%.
Reversion improved to -1.2% in 1H2026 from -24.5% for the full FY2025.
The periods differ, but a move into positive territory would be worth noting.
CLCT also saved 16% on interest YoY.
Aggregate leverage improved to 40.4% from 42.1%, with the average cost of debt at 3.06%.
A higher realised foreign exchange loss offset part of these gains, so watch the
currency line
on 23 October.
Related articles:
3 High-Yielding REITs Paying Over 6.5%: Bargains or Traps?
3 Singapore REITs, 3 Different Stories: What the FY2025 Results Really Tell Us
Get Smart: Find what filled the gap
DPU tells you what unitholders received.
NPI tells you what the properties earned.
When the two move apart, find out why before deciding whether the trend will last.
When these three REITs report, put the DPU change next to the NPI change.
If the gap is wide, look for the bridge.
Interest savings and one-off items can lift DPU growth above NPI growth for a while.
Then, ask the really important question: ask whether that bridge will still be there next year.

title: Qatar LNG cargo makes rare Red Sea journey to get gas to Europe
article:
(Oct 19): A carrier loaded with Qatari liquefied natural gas (LNG) is sailing north through the Red Sea, potentially speeding up delivery to European customers with a rare transit through waters vulnerable to renewed attacks from Houthi rebels.

The tanker, which loaded an LNG cargo in Qatar in August, is signalling Poland as its next destination, according to ship-tracking data compiled by Bloomberg. Poland’s Orlen SA has a long-term supply contract with QatarEnergy, though shipments under the deal were cancelled after the exporter’s giant Ras Laffan plant was hit by drone strikes in March.

The transit — which comes as European natural gas prices hit the highest level in almost four years — is unusual. Commercial vessels have increasingly tended to take long detours to avoid the Red Sea, typically sailing around Africa’s Cape of Good Hope to head to Europe, a route that can add almost two weeks and extra costs to a one-way journey.

UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO), a security outfit which links commercial shipping and military forces, reported on Saturday that an unnamed LNG tanker was approached southeast of the Yemeni port of Al Mukalla, in the Gulf of Aden, by a skiff that fired two shots. The tanker’s security team fired two shots in return.

UKMTO did not provide further details, though ship-tracking data suggest the Poland-bound carrier was the only LNG tanker in the region at the time. The data suggests the vessel has since continued its journey.

QatarEnergy did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

See also: Exxon signals record refining earnings on soaring diesel prices

Continued disruption around the Strait of Hormuz has tightened global LNG supply for months, driving up prices and forcing Middle Eastern suppliers to look for workarounds.

This latest Qatari cargo is heading to Europe at a time when the continent has struggled to refill its gas inventories ahead of winter. Reserves of the fuel are sitting at the lowest seasonal level in over a decade, threatening even higher prices as temperatures begin to drop.

title: JPMorgan brings deposit token to ethereum for institutional clients
article:
(Oct 19): JPMorgan Chase & Co is launching its deposit token on ethereum, extending the lender’s push into blockchain payments as Wall Street grows more comfortable moving money on public networks.

JPM Coin — which represents US dollar deposits at the largest US bank — will be made available to the company’s institutional clients on the ethereum network, JPMorgan said in a statement on Monday. First launched last year on Coinbase Global Inc-affiliated blockchain base, the deposit token allows clients to send and receive money in seconds and 24/7, rather than over several days and only during working hours.

The bank expects JPM Coin to be used by large clients in the cryptocurrency sector seeking a way to make payments on blockchain, as well as financial institutions that need a form of digital cash to settle or collateralise transactions of tokenised assets, Emma Landriault, global head of Kinexys Labs at JPMorgan’s blockchain division Kinexys, said in an interview.

Tokenisation allows traditional assets such as stocks, bonds and funds to be represented and transferred via blockchain networks. While banks have spent more than a decade exploring the technology’s potential, a lot of the work to date has focused on private networks, where access is restricted and banks retain greater control over participants.

Moving onto public infrastructure — albeit with limits on who can hold the tokens — brings Wall Street closer to the crypto ecosystem, enabling them to tap into existing pools of liquidity and developer activity.

“We’ve clearly been in a year of further convergence between Wall Street and crypto,” Landriault said. “It’s not just Wall Street going to public chains, but the institutional web3 players getting more embedded and partnering with traditional financial institutions.” JPM Coin’s move onto ethereum underscores that shift, she added.

See also: Crypto wallet tampering fallout widens as OneKey drops Malaysian reseller

The bank chose to bring the token to ethereum because of its liquidity and existing use among clients, Landriault said. Ethereum is the largest blockchain by the total value of assets locked into it, with about US$50 billion deposited in applications running on the network, according to DefiLlama data.

JPMorgan’s expansion comes as banks and other large financial firms seek ways to move assets faster and beyond the limitations of traditional systems by using crypto’s underlying technology. A company backed by more than 100 corporations including Visa Inc, Stripe Inc, and Mastercard Inc issued a US dollar-pegged stablecoin last month, another form of digital money.

JPMorgan is one of the more active banks in blockchain development. It also runs the Kinexys Blockchain Deposit Account network, which allows corporate clients to move dollars, euros, pounds and several other currencies, on the bank’s private blockchain. The network processes more than US$7 billion in transactions a day, JPMorgan said, a sliver of the roughly US$12 trillion a day its broader payments division handles daily.

title: Morgan Stanley enters UK savings market with Raisin partnership
article:
(Oct 19): Morgan Stanley is partnering with fintech platform Raisin UK to roll out savings accounts to individuals, following similar moves in Germany and the Netherlands.

Starting this week, the Wall Street bank is offering fixed-term deposits at interest rates as high as 5.1%, with a minimum deposit of £1,000 (US$1,334), the company said in a statement Monday. Over time, Morgan Stanley will look at other potential partners and products, according to people familiar with the matter.

The move is part of the bank’s deposit-gathering strategy and doesn’t reflect a wider push into UK consumer or retail banking, said the people, who asked not to be named as the details aren’t public.

“The UK is one of the world’s largest and most established savings markets,” Christopher Beatty, Morgan Stanley’s chief operating officer for Europe, the Middle East and Africa, said in a statement.

In the US, Morgan Stanley offers savings accounts to clients with brokerage accounts. In September, the bank entered the Netherlands via Raisin, following a similar partnership in Germany in 2025.

The UK savings market has been dominated by high street lenders including Lloyds Banking Group Plc and Nationwide Building Society, though Wall Street firms have entered the market in recent years.

See also: PHP agrees £700 mil UK private hospital venture with GIC

JPMorgan Chase & Co opened Chase in the UK in 2021 before expanding into savings products, then moving into Germany earlier this year. Goldman Sachs Group Inc’s retail bank Marcus started UK operations in 2018. Goldman has also begun hiring staff to assess the viability of launching Marcus in Ireland.

Morgan Stanley’s new offering compares to similar accounts at rivals such as Marcus, which offers a one-year fixed term account at 4.75%.

title: PHP agrees £700 mil UK private hospital venture with GIC
article:
(Oct 19): Primary Health properties Plc has formed a £700 million (US$933 million) venture with GIC Pte Ltd, part of its ongoing plan to reduce debt levels following a merger last year.

The UK healthcare landlord will seed the venture with 27 private hospitals, according to a statement Monday. As part of the deal, PHP will receive about £500 million, which will be used to repay the bridging loan it used to finance the takeover of rival Assura, and another debt facility. This will reduce PHP’s net debt to about £2.9 billion.

While Europe’s property markets continue to suffer in the face of high bond yields, infrastructure-like assets that have offer secure long-term income and can help hedge against inflation have been a relative bright spot. Demand for private healthcare in the UK has been increasing as pressure on public services grows, leading to lengthy delays for treatment.

“In addition to generating proceeds to reduce our borrowings, the transaction enhances returns on invested equity for our shareholders and brings a highly aligned capital partner to support investment in essential UK hospital infrastructure,” said Mark Davies, chief executive officer at PHP.

Last year, PHP outbid KKR & Co to buy Assura in a combination that created one of the UK’s largest publicly traded landlords. The listed real estate market has continued to shrink this year after Prologis Inc secured a deal to takeover the UK’s largest listed real estate company, Segro Plc.

Rothschild & Co acted as financial adviser to PHP.

See also: Vietnam plans index options for next year after FTSE upgrade

title: Dubai sweetens first IPO since war with US$592 mil dividend
article:
(Oct 19): DIP Holding PLC is trying to rustle up demand for the United Arab Emirates’ first initial public offering since the Iran war began by offering investors dividend payouts worth US$592 million over the next three years.

The firm’s sole owner, Dubai Investments PJSC, plans to sell 20% of the company’s shares, according to terms of the deal seen by Bloomberg News. DIP Holding owns Dubai Investments Park, one of the UAE’s largest mixed-use developments.

The subscription period will run from Oct 27 to Nov 3, with trading expected to start on Nov 11 on Dubai’s bourse. Bloomberg News reported the firm’s plans to start investor meetings last week.

Beyond DIP Holding, Dubai Investments has stakes in about 30 companies spanning manufacturing, real estate and financial services. Shares in the parent company rose as much as 5.1%, the most since early May.

The firm expects to pay annualised dividends of 700 million dirhams (US$190.58 million) in 2026, and 725 million dirhams and 750 million dirhams in 2027 and 2028 respectively.

The 2,300-hectare (8.9-square miles) DIP was established in 1997 and includes warehouses, hotels, retail outlets, schools and medical centres.

See also: Mi Material launches IPO at $1.80 each, aims to raise gross proceeds of $168.2 mil

Citigroup Inc, Emirates NBD Capital and HSBC Holdings Plc are the joint global coordinators on the deal, with Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank, Arqaam, Dubai Islamic Bank and EFG Hermes mandated as joint bookrunners.

Once a hub for IPOs, Gulf listing volumes have slumped this year as the regional war deepens a broader market slowdown. Equity markets across the region have fallen since the conflict began, with Oman the sole exception, while Dubai’s benchmark index is down about 9%.

title: Nidec legal reckoning reaches founder, shares hit decade low
article:
(Oct 19): Nidec Corp shares fell to their lowest in a decade after an outside committee concluded that founder Shigenobu Nagamori and other current or former executives bear civil liability for damages linked to years of improper accounting.

The finding, which was submitted to the board last week, deepens a crisis that has prompted the motor maker’s biggest shareholder to call for a review of privatisation options. Nidec plans to publish a partially redacted version of the report on Tuesday.

While the announcement marks a break with Nidec’s founder-dominated past, it also raises questions over whether the company’s cleanup effort still has a long way to go. The manufacturer is seeking to regain auditor approval and convince the Tokyo Stock Exchange that its internal controls have been repaired. At the same time, newly appointed chief executive officer Michio Kaida needs to restructure loss-making businesses and respond to activist pressure.

Nidec shares fell to their lowest since 2016 on Monday. The stock has lost more than a third of its value since late September, when Nidec announced the sudden exit of Mitsuya Kishida as CEO. The motor manufacturer now has a market value of ¥2.1 trillion ($17 billion), compared with almost ¥9 trillion less than six years ago.

Nidec said it recognised that multiple directors and other executives violated corporate laws and regulations while carrying out their duties and would consider claims for damages and other legal measures, then respond swiftly. The committee said the amount of any damages should be determined according to each person’s contribution.

Apart from Nagamori, the report on Friday named former CEOs Jun Seki and Kishida, former chairman Hiroshi Kobe, former President Hiroyuki Yoshimoto and former senior vice-president Akira Sato. Kazuya Murakami, identified by the committee as one of those bearing liability, was listed as the company’s chief legal officer and head of compliance as of Oct 1. Nidec said he is no longer employed at the company.

See also: BOJ to lean against back-to-back rate hike in October — Bloomberg

The scope of any damages to be claimed should be determined according to their degree of contribution, Nidec said in the statement. The latest finding could help Kaida demonstrate that Nidec’s board is willing to hold its former leaders accountable.

Nidec has been designated a security on special alert since October 2025 because of the need to improve its internal management system. Accounting auditor PwC Japan withheld its opinion on the accounts after saying it was unable to obtain sufficient and appropriate evidence. The company is seeking to obtain the auditor’s sign-off and submit a report to the exchange by Oct 28 as it seeks to avoid a delisting notice.

Oasis Management Co disclosed last week that its stake in Nidec had risen to 9%, making it the largest disclosed shareholder and placing it ahead of Nagamori’s direct holding. Oasis founder Seth Fischer has urged Nidec’s outside directors to hire financial advisers and seek preliminary, non-binding proposals as protection against an unintended delisting.

See also: Topix’s biggest ever revamp to cull hundreds of Japan stocks

Nagamori built Nidec through decades of aggressive acquisitions and a high-pressure operating culture, but struggled to hand over control. Yoshimoto and Seki were each tapped as potential successors before leaving, while Nagamori retained influence over the company. He relinquished his last formal title in February but remains one of Nidec’s largest shareholders.

The accounting fallout has devastated Nidec’s finances. It reported a ¥519 billion operating loss for the year ended March after recording a ¥632 billion impairment. The company forecast a return to ¥200 billion in profit on ¥2.8 trillion of sales in the current fiscal year.

The legal claims and ongoing uncertainty over the accounts and a potential delisting may also complicate a sale of the company. Any buyer would have to assess the legal claims, audit questions and whether Nagamori, who remains a major shareholder, would support any transaction.

title: Foxconn buys US$727 mil stake in Mitsubishi Electric unit making EV parts
article:
(Oct 19): Hon Hai Precision Industry Co is paying ¥115 billion (US$727 million) for a 50% stake in Mitsubishi Electric Corp’s automotive-components unit, with the goal of turning it into a business with more than ¥1 trillion in sales.

Mitsubishi will contribute technology in electric powertrains, autonomous driving and in-car intelligence for EV platforms developed by Hon Hai, better known as Foxconn, the companies said Monday during a news conference in Tokyo.

The tie-up gives Foxconn a deeper foothold in the auto industry as it pushes its contract-manufacturing model into EVs, while giving Mitsubishi Electric a partner to help scale its car-parts business. The companies plan to combine Mitsubishi’s long-standing relationships with automakers with Foxconn’s faster development model, while broadening the business beyond traditional auto components into EV and autonomous-driving platforms.

“What attracted us most was the electronic-control technology — and the substantial software resources behind them,” Jun Seki, Foxconn’s chief strategy officer for EVs, said at the event.

The deal values the new automotive business at ¥320 billion on an enterprise-value basis. The unit generated ¥876 billion in revenue and ¥54 billion in operating profit in the year ended March.

Mitsubishi Electric expects to book an impairment charge of about ¥100 billion this fiscal year as a result of the transaction. It plans to update its full-year earnings forecast on Oct 30.

See also: UniCredit gets ECB go-ahead to take control of Commerzbank

The companies expect the transaction to be completed in October 2027. The parts business will then become a 50-50 venture and cease to be a consolidated Mitsubishi Electric subsidiary.

title: Thailand targets US$417 mil of land in foreign buyer crackdown
article:
(Oct 19): Thailand is moving to force the sale of land worth about 14 billion baht (US$417 million or $530 million) as it cracks down on foreigners who evade an ownership ban by holding property via local proxies.

Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul said on Monday that his government is stepping up investigations into such arrangements and tightening scrutiny of new purchases.

Foreigners are prohibited from owning land in Thailand, but some use Thai nominees to circumvent the restrictions, a practice under growing scrutiny after a series of cases in major tourist and business centres.

Authorities are targeting about 5,467 rai (2,161 acres) of land linked to suspected nominee arrangements, according to Somchai Leelanoy, director-general of the Department of Lands. That is an area roughly equivalent to 1,225 standard soccer fields.

Anutin ordered officials to accelerate investigations of high-risk cases by December and enforce laws requiring illegally held land to be sold. Authorities will also seek to prevent new nominee arrangements from entering the property system, he said at a briefing Monday.

The government is tightening checks on buyers as part of the effort. Individuals purchasing land for more than two million baht, or property with an assessed value exceeding five million baht, will face background checks, Somchai said.

See also: Bukit Sembawang to acquire Kallang Distripark land from other Lee-family entities for $196 mil

Thai nationals married to foreigners will have to show that money used to purchase land belongs to the Thai spouse. Companies buying property will face scrutiny of their shareholders and sources of funds and be required to provide supporting documents under Thailand’s land laws.

title: Malaysia's September exports surge to five-year high on AI demand
article:
(Oct 19): Malaysia’s exports surged to its highest level in more than five years in September as the trade-dependent nation continues to benefit from demand for artificial intelligence-related products.

Exports rose 54.5% in September from a year earlier, the highest since April 2021, and exceeding the 39.9% estimate in a Bloomberg survey.

The growth was boosted by higher exports of electrical and electronic products, valued at RM45 billion (US$11 billion) in September, the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) said in a statement Monday.

Shipments to the US surged 89.9%, and exports to China were up 22.1% for the month, according to the department.

Imports rose 52.7% in September from a year ago, higher than the 39% forecast in a Bloomberg survey.

Malaysia recorded a trade surplus of RM33.7 billion in September, above the RM31.6 billion surplus in the Bloomberg survey.

See also: Malaysia's King Sultan Ibrahim acquires 2.25% in Southern Alliance Mining in $6.1 mil offmarket deal

Demand for electronics used in AI have helped cushion Malaysia from global disruptions. The Southeast Asian country’s economy expanded 5.3% in the three months through September from a year earlier.

Exports in the third quarter rose 46%, the statistics department said. Malaysia’s total trade increased 30.1% from January to September compared to the same period a year ago, with exports up 34%.

The country’s consumer prices were up 1.8% in September from a year earlier, below the 1.9% forecast in a Bloomberg survey, according to separate data from the statistic department on Monday.

title: Vietnam plans index options for next year after FTSE upgrade
article:
(Oct 19): Vietnam aims to introduce stock index options in the first quarter of next year as the country seeks to deepen its capital markets and attract more overseas investors following an upgrade to its equity market.

Testing of contracts tied to the VN30 Index is scheduled for November and December, Vu Thi Thuy Nga, general director of the Hanoi Stock Exchange, said in an interview. The gauge comprises the 30 largest stocks by market value on the Ho Chi Minh City Stock Exchange.

The new derivatives products are being introduced to lure more foreign capital into Vietnamese shares after FTSE Russell upgraded the country to secondary emerging-market status from frontier effective last month. The reclassification is expected to broaden Vietnam’s access to global emerging-market investment, even as the transition is phased in, with inclusion in FTSE’s emerging-market indexes expected through 2027.

The authorities expect the new options to help increase trading activity and improve liquidity, potentially supporting broader participation in the market, Hanoi Stock Exchange’s Nga said.

“This is a highly anticipated product, and it is hoped that it will help the market take off,” she said. “Now that we have been upgraded, we need products that align with those of more developed exchanges.”

See also: Australia regulator halts another credit fund amid crackdown

Vietnam has undertaken a number of reforms in recent years to improve market accessibility.

Authorities have removed pre-funding requirements for equity trades, advanced plans for a centralised clearing system by 2027 and allowed foreign investors to trade via global brokerages, among other measures. The country is also weighing plans to allow trading during the midday break and widen daily price bands to improve liquidity.

The VN30 Index gained 5.9% in August amid optimism over the FTSE update before dropping 3.8% in September.

title: China’s growth rebound tops forecasts to close in on target
article:
(Oct 19): China’s growth accelerated more than expected in the third quarter, boosting the odds of the economy reaching Beijing’s annual target and dimming the prospects for additional easing measures.

Gross domestic product (GDP) grew 4.5% from a year ago after a gain of 4.3% in the second quarter, according to data released by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) on Monday, compared with the median forecast of 4.4% by economists surveyed by Bloomberg. That took expansion in the first nine months of the year to 4.6% — within the government’s annual goal of 4.5%-5%.

The improvement in the economy should give policymakers some breathing room, allowing them to hold off on further easing as they remain constrained by thin bank margins and persistent fiscal strain on local governments.

Industrial production growth accelerated to 5.5% on year in September, matching forecasts. Fixed-asset investment shrank 7.2% in the first nine months of the year, unchanged from its drop in January-August.

Retail sales picked up far more than expected to 1.1%, versus a 0.4% rise in August. Excluding car purchases, retail sales grew 3.9% from a year ago, the fastest pace since October 2025.

See also: Chinese stocks turn biggest losers as global AI trade stumbles

“Bigger fiscal spending helped both fixed-asset investment and retail sales,” said Xing Zhaopeng, senior China strategist at Australia & New Zealand Banking Group Ltd. “The recovery remains unsolid because the fiscal outlook is not stable. The question will be how much fiscal expansion can do in the future. We still see a downside risk to 2027.”

The yield on the government’s 10-year bonds climbed one basis point to 1.65% after the data release. The yuan held on to its earlier gain, rising 0.1% to 6.6829 per dollar in offshore trading.

China’s currency has advanced over 4% against the greenback since the start of the year to outperform most of its Asian peers, thanks to rising exports and the central bank’s tolerance for a stronger exchange rate.

See also: China plans AI tech export curbs to manage security risks

With industrial output growing at the fastest since March in a sign of China’s supply-side “strength,” the government’s support for the economy will likely “stay at the current level with only a marginal adjustment,” said Helen Qiao, chief economist for greater China at BofA Global Research.

Even as the slowdown intensified in recent months, officials initially focused on implementing existing pro-growth policies, before dialing up their support three weeks ago with a package of fresh targeted measures.

Growth in the world’s second-largest economy has been marked by a divide between booming exports — stoked by a global investment supercycle in artificial intelligence — and sluggish household spending, with investment stuck in a long slump. The job market has also softened while a years-long property downturn drags on.

Property investment plunged 20.6% in the first nine months and capital spending on infrastructure slumped 4.2%, a deterioration from their performance in January-August. The surveyed urban jobless rate unexpectedly improved to 5.2% in September from 5.3% in the prior month.

Frail domestic demand has left China increasingly dependent on exports for growth. And that’s put Beijing under rising pressure from trade partners to address its yawning surplus, which is on pace to hit a new high this year in excess of the US$1.2 trillion recorded in 2025.

The European Union is preparing to create new powers that could allow it to shut off China’s access to its single market as part of a dramatic new push to rebalance bilateral trade.

Meanwhile, foreign leaders have called on Beijing to allow for more appreciation in the Chinese currency, which they say is undervalued and gives the nation’s exporters an unfair competitive advantage. The International Monetary Fund estimates the yuan’s undervaluation in the range of 17.3% to 25.3% in 2026, with a midpoint of 21.3%.

“Overall, the latest data suggest growth momentum improved towards the end of the third quarter,” said Zhou Hao, chief economist at Guotai Junan. “While the property downturn and soft domestic demand remain challenging, stronger-than-expected GDP and retail sales figures, firmer manufacturing activity, and an improving labour market point to a more constructive outlook for this quarter.”

title: ECB’s Sleijpen says window is closing to limit warming impact
article:
(Oct 19): European Central Bank (ECB) Governing Council member Olaf Sleijpen said that the chance to limit global warming to the limit envisaged by the Paris Agreement is almost spent.

“Scientific evidence shows that the remaining carbon budget consistent with limiting global warming to 1.5°C is now almost exhausted,” Sleijpen said in Manila on Monday. “We are no longer choosing between success and failure, but between an outcome that is bad but still manageable, and an outcome that we can no longer manage.”

Sleijpen spoke in his capacity as chair of the Network for Greening the Financial System, a club of global monetary authorities. He also heads the Dutch central bank.

title: Japan PM Takaichi denies she’s driving weak yen, high rates
article:
(Oct 19): Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi strongly denied the notion that she’s responsible for a weak yen and high interest rates.

“Up until now, I’ve been criticised a lot for things like ‘Takaichi’s weak yen’ and ‘Takaichi’s high interest rates’,” she said in parliament on Monday. “I categorically reject those claims.”

Her administration aims to boost confidence in the yen by building a strong economy and achieving fiscal sustainability, Takaichi said, adding that that she will appropriately control the issuance of Japanese government bonds in next fiscal year’s budget.

The premier’s comments come as her year-old administration tries to ease persistent market unease about its fiscal management. Earlier this year, drafts of an annual economic policy blueprint fuelled concerns that the government was shifting towards a more expansionary stance, sending the yen lower versus the dollar and long-term sovereign debt yields higher.

However, Growth Strategy Minister Minoru Kiuchi said in September that Japan no longer needs a reflationary policy of aggressive monetary easing and fiscal spending. Takaichi made similar remarks earlier this month. Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama has said Takaichi isn’t a reflationist, a label the prime minister has long been associated with.

Market participants are paying close attention to how the government will fund a planned sales tax cut on food and higher defence spending without worsening the nation’s debt burden.

See also: Ueda ‘can’t tolerate’ underlying inflation further over 2%

Separately, Bank of Japan (BOJ) governor Kazuo Ueda, who appeared with Takaichi in parliament, said underlying inflation is rising very close to the bank’s 2% target. The governor also said that long-term bond yields may rise if the market perceives that the BOJ is not raising the benchmark policy interest rate at an appropriate pace.

title: Meta says Claude AI tool triggered No Kings Instagram suspension
article:
(Oct 19): Meta Platforms Inc said an automated security system mistakenly suspended the Instagram account of the No Kings Coalition at the height of a nationwide series of demonstrations.

The technology company offered an apology and a more detailed explanation for the disruption, which came during the group’s early-voting push ahead of the Nov 3 midterm elections.

Instagram’s engineering team found that the accounts’ “reading” activity triggered the security system. A tool from Anthropic PBC’s Claude was accessing profiles, posts and hashtags at roughly four times the normal rate in intense bursts Saturday, Andy Stone, Meta’s vice president of communications wrote in a social media post Sunday.

“These abrupt, high-volume, sequential requests in a short period resembled automated bot traffic rather than an ordinary human browsing our systems,” Stone said.

Meta said an automated review about an hour later determined the account shouldn’t have been removed and restored it, though it took longer to return administrative access.

“We want to reiterate our sincere apology for the error,” Stone said.

See also: China’s CXMT swings to profit after memory chip prices surge

The No Kings Coalition, an anti-Trump group, said Saturday that its Instagram page was unavailable for about 90 minutes and that organisers remained locked out of the account even after it became publicly visible again. Full access was restored at 5:33pm New York time on Saturday, according to the coalition.

Organisers criticised Meta for restricting the account during the demonstrations, saying Instagram was a crucial platform for communicating with supporters.

The coalition said millions of people participated in nearly 3,000 events in all 50 states and Washington in an effort to expand early vote access and defend election integrity.

See also: Apple iPhone Duo orders slip into 2027 amid pre-order frenzy

Stone’s statement on Sunday didn’t specify which Claude tool was involved, who was operating it or what activity it had been carrying out in connection with the account. No Kings did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The explanation clarified Meta’s initial account of the incident. Stone said Saturday that unusually high rates of posting, sharing or commenting had triggered the company’s automated systems and that such activity had caused the No Kings account to be suspended. He called the action “clearly” an error.

No Kings, which has organised several anti-Trump protests since he was inaugurated, said it plans a national organising call Wednesday focused on turnout ahead of Election Day.

title: CPA Australia prepares future-ready accounting and finance leaders
article:
Like most other vocations, accounting and finance are being reshaped by technology. Coupled with expanded business responsibilities and changing workforce needs, the skills essential for success are quickly evolving.

According to some CPA Australia members, accounting and finance professionals are expected to not just be bookkeepers, but also strategic advisors to organisations.

Lee Soon Wee CPA (Aust.), group financial controller at global offshore and marine giant, Seatrium, says that the growing adoption of AI and automation is accelerating this shift, with technology complementing human expertise and enabling finance teams to focus on creating long-term value for the business.

“Today, finance teams are increasingly relied upon to provide deeper insights, strengthen governance and support decision-making for stakeholders, including senior management and investors,” shares Lee. “With routine activities increasingly automated with AI adoption, finance professionals can devote more time to higher-value work such as forecasting, risk management, performance analysis and supporting strategic business decisions.”

Echoing similar observations, Ayo Canlas CPA (Aust.), CFO of SharkNinja APAC, says that accountants are asked to deliver greater value to their organisations.

“I am seeing a common thread where routine accounting tasks are now automated so that finance professionals can contribute not just from a finance point of view, but also towards commercial insights as well,” points out Canlas.

Technical knowledge in accounting is not enough to excel in the contemporary business world.

According to the Future of Jobs 2025 report by the World Economic Forum (WEF), employers expect technological advancements in areas such as AI and information processing, and robotics and automation, to be “transformative”, with nearly two-fifths of workers’ skills to become outdated between 2025 and 2030.

Technology-related skills, in particular AI and big data, were ranked top of the fastest growing skills.

Meanwhile, analytical thinking was found to be the most sought-after core skill, with creative thinking, resilience, flexibility and agility, along with curiosity and lifelong learning, expected to become more important in the years to come.

For Canlas, accountants must be tech-savvy and able to leverage technology to free up time for higher-value work, including developing stronger business acumen and other critical skills.

“So how do you take advantage of that unique point of view? You can already see what's happening in the business through a financial lens. The next step is using those insights and take that us one or two steps forward, and contribute meaningfully to commercial discussions and strategic decision-making,” he shares.

As one of SharkNinja’s first few employees in Singapore, Canlas had to contribute to charting the regional growth of the company, which is outside the traditional accounting job scope.

“For example, management will ask how to use past financial data to develop a three-to-five-year plan,” he explains. “That's a good example of something that is beyond keeping the books.”

Meanwhile, Lee adds that emotional intelligence is another essential skill for business leaders.

“EQ is also quite an important factor in our day-to-day professional life. When you’re in the office, you have to interact with other people like your CEO, your board of directors, colleagues, among others.”

Highlighting the importance for accountants to have more than technical accounting skills to grow beyond their traditional role, Lee shares his experience on a merger and acquisition transaction where he was part of the negotiation team.

“Imagine an accountant sitting across the negotiation table; it is not a matter of reading from a script. You have to apply negotiation skills, interpersonal skills, and stay on top of what's going on around you,” he says.

“You have to read the other party’s body language, be mindful of what you say and how you say it. So, these are certain soft skills, beyond accounting that you need to be very mindful of.”

Beyond the comfort zone and textbook

As evidenced by their experiences, both Canlas and Lee went out of their way to take on responsibilities beyond traditional accounting to grow in their careers.

Starting out in audit, Lee contributed in other areas including commercial strategy and initiatives. These experiences provided him with opportunities to grow and excel.

“I got exposure to mergers and acquisitions. In particular, I experienced the merger between two of the largest shipyards in Singapore, Keppel Offshore and Marine and Sembcorp Marine, to establish Seatrium,” he says.

“These are learning opportunities that are not found in textbooks.”

Lee adds that Seatrium views AI as a tool that empowers employees to create greater value, and has deployed it across the firm’s corporate functions to augment employees' capabilities and improve productivity. Within finance, AI helps automate routine and time-intensive tasks, enabling teams to generate reports more efficiently and focus on higher-value work such as analysis, business partnering, risk management and strategic decision-making.

For a global business like Seatrium, operating across 15 countries, technology provides greater visibility and control across its operations, helping the company to improve efficiency, consistency and transparency, shares Lee.

Meanwhile, Canlas shares that he spearheads the AI and data team in SharkNinja. Through his efforts, data is now more accessible across departments, enabling wider collaboration with more in-depth evidence and analysis that drives better and comprehensive business decisions.

“The different teams I'm leading are also benefitting from the broader investment in AI, because they now see better the connections between finance, strategy, business planning and analytics,” he says.

“When we think about managing risks and opportunities, we're not constrained to just financial data. We can see the bigger picture.”

Canlas is guided by the mindset of being a “business leader first, functional leader second”. This means one should understand business priorities and apply technical and functional knowledge to fulfil those business priorities.

Lee adds, “As the profession continues to evolve along with technological developments, finance leaders will need to combine financial expertise, business acumen and digital capabilities to support better business outcomes."

The value of the CPA qualification

While both Canlas and Lee believe in the importance of on-the-job learning, they also value the training and rigour of the CPA Program in supporting finance professionals to advance their career aspirations.

"As technology and AI continue to reshape the profession, the CPA Program equips finance professionals with not only strong technical foundations, but also leadership, governance, digital finance, analytical thinking and problem-solving capabilities needed to thrive in an increasingly complex business environment," Lee elaborates.

“It also suggests a growth mindset and a certain level of discipline, as maintaining the designation requires one to fulfil the requisite hours of continuous professional development (CPD).”

Echoing his fellow CPA designation holder, Canlas says: “It’s a designation that helps to ensure that the fundamentals are strong. In that case, it’s been critical for our hiring especially for technical roles.

“CPA Australia’s focus on the skills and knowledge that matter most to the profession helps me achieve two objectives at once. While supporting my team to meet their CPD requirements, it also helps strengthen their commercial mindset and broader business acumen.”

Another much appreciated aspect of becoming a CPA is the mentorship and broader career opportunities provided by CPA Australia.

“You get insights from mentors who share their real-world experiences,” says Lee.

He also adds that global recognition of the CPA designation opens doors for members to pursue overseas career opportunities and gain valuable international perspectives.

To Canlas, events and workshops organised by the Singapore Division not only provide professional training, but they also facilitate networking, allowing members to exchange insights and explore potential opportunities.

With many members becoming finance leaders or working beyond traditional accounting functions in areas such as sustainability, technology, banking, consulting, risk management and executive leadership, both Canlas and Lee agree that the CPA qualification is a stepping stone for accountants and finance professionals aspiring to elevate their careers to new heights.

“It's a designation that brings a lot of pride, but with that, it's also a lot of responsibility,” says Canlas.

Lee notes that the CPA designation is a signifier of a qualified finance professional.

“Professional qualifications such as CPA Australia provide a strong indication of an individual's technical expertise, professional rigour and commitment to continuous learning, all of which are valuable qualities when assessing candidates.”

Enrolments for the CPA Program Semester 1 2027 open on Monday 30 November. For those looking to accelerate their professional growth, register for the Become a CPA information sessions to learn how the CPA Program can equip you with the knowledge, networks and professional recognition needed to thrive in a rapidly evolving business environment.

title: Brent crude holds near US$110 on Mideast and Ukraine conflicts
article:
(Oct 19) : Oil steadied after jumping on Friday, as flareups in fighting in the Middle East and Ukraine dimmed the prospect of a return to normal crude flows.

Brent traded below US$110 a barrel after Friday hitting the milestone for the first time since May, West Texas Intermediate was near US$101 and European natural gas jumped as much as 2%. In the Middle East, a Saudi helicopter crashed near the border with Yemen and Houthi rebels targeted Yanbu, a crucial export hub, while UK maritime operations said two tankers reported being hit in the Persian Gulf.

Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump said he cut a diesel export deal with Russia and delayed imposing further sanctions to preserve peace talks with Ukraine. US lawmakers introduced a bill on Friday to block the deal, which has also been criticized by Republicans. Moscow and Kyiv traded tit-for-tat attacks on energy infrastructure.

Brent has surged about 80% this year as the widening hostilities in the two regions revived concerns over supply. Physical markets continue to signal tightness and refined products such as diesel have rallied even harder, with European futures for the commodity more than doubling this year.

“Mounting attacks on energy infrastructure and vessels are eroding hopes of a sustained recovery in oil flows,” said Jorge Leon, head of geopolitical analysis at Rystad Energy. “The market is increasingly pricing in a longer disruption, with risks to prices tilted to the upside heading into the week.”

Nevertheless, barrels do seem to be exiting the Persian Gulf. The US said over the weekend that its forces helped escort more than 100 million barrels of oil through the Strait of Hormuz over the prior week.

See also: US stock futures rise ahead of busy earnings week

title: US stock futures rise ahead of busy earnings week
article:
(Oct 19) : US stock futures rose and oil edged lower as traders prepared for a packed week of corporate earnings and Chinese economic data against a backdrop of heightened geopolitical risks.

Futures on the S&P 500 Index advanced, erasing earlier losses after the underlying gauge fell 1.1% Friday, capping its worst week since June. The VIX Index jumped to a four-month intraday high on Friday as technology shares slumped, while the dollar was mixed against major peers in early trading.

More than 70 S&P 500 companies are due to report this week, including Magnificent Seven members Tesla Inc. and Meta Platforms Inc., putting the durability of the artificial-intelligence trade back in the spotlight. In Asia, a swath of Chinese economic data Monday will offer fresh clues on the health of the world’s second-largest economy.

Brent crude fell 0.7% after climbing Friday, with oil near US$110 a barrel adding to inflation concerns and complicating the outlook for interest rates. The Federal Reserve has entered its communications blackout period ahead of its Oct. 28 policy decision, while geopolitical risks remained elevated as relations between the US and Ukraine deteriorated.

Investors are bracing for further swings across stocks and bonds as questions grow over whether massive spending on AI infrastructure will deliver sufficient returns. A measure of bond volatility also remains elevated, while persistent fuel and food inflation is adding pressure on central banks.

We’re in “a classic period of heightened uncertainty,” said Kyle Rodda, a senior analyst at Capital.com in Melbourne. “Several things are colliding at the same time. AI earnings are coming up, interest rate uncertainty is persistent and the midterms are a few weeks away. For Asia, the impacts will be more acute given that all of these themes are amplified because of exposure to chips, higher yields and energy prices.”

See also: MSCI weighs downgrade of Indonesia to remove from global indexes

Treasuries, which had been favored as a haven during the technology selloff, came under pressure Friday as oil climbed. Brent rose at the end of last week on doubts over US President Donald Trump’s deal to release more Russian diesel into global markets and supply disruptions stretching from the Strait of Hormuz to the Black Sea.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Trump of trying to pressure Kyiv into surrendering to Russia, escalating a week-long row with the US president.

“I am in the process of negotiating Peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine, and don’t want to do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table. Great progress is being made,” Trump wrote in a social-media post.

See also: Stock buyers step in to power Wall Street rebound

Elsewhere, the euro lagged major peers as protests in several French cities descended into clashes between police and demonstrators, with looting and landmarks set on fire. Demonstrations also took place in Belgium, Italy and Portugal.

Chinese assets will be closely watched after authorities moved last week to shore up the equity market by urging companies and state funds to buy shares and guiding some investors to curb selling. The measures followed a technology-driven slump that sent the CSI 300 Index to its lowest since August 2025.

Monday’s data, including third-quarter gross domestic product, will provide fresh clues on China’s outlook. Economists surveyed by Bloomberg expect growth to rebound slightly, though weak consumption, sluggish private investment and a prolonged property downturn remain drags.

Investors will also look for signs of additional policy support as top financial officials, including People’s Bank of China Governor Pan Gongsheng, speak at the 2026 Financial Street Forum starting Monday. Easing bets have increased, with China’s one-year interest-rate swap falling last week to its lowest since April 2020.

“We expect a continuation of the ‘two-speed economy’ of strong industrial production for exports and weak growth in domestic demand,” Commonwealth Bank of Australia strategists led by Joseph Capurso wrote in a note.
